_comment: wifipilot configuration. Copy to wifipilot.json (or pass --config) and edit. Every value can also be overridden per run on the command line; `wifipilot config` prints the effective merged configuration.
_engagement: stealth=true never transmits (no deauth, no online PIN attacks). aggressive controls whether clients are deauthenticated to force a handshake.
_attacks: Valid (27): ie_audit, pnl_harvest, pmkid, pmkid_flood, handshake, eapol_logoff, wps_pixie, wps_pin, wep_ivs, wep_p0841, wep_chopchop, wep_fragment, wep_hirte, hidden_ssid, tracker, rogue_ap, enterprise, rogue_radius, saewolf, pmf_audit, evil_twin, karma, deauth_flood, auth_flood, probe_flood, beacon_flood, passive.  Read-only (no authorisation needed for the listening part): ie_audit (decode the beacon elements), pnl_harvest (what clients are asking for), pmf_audit, saewolf, hidden_ssid, tracker, rogue_ap, enterprise.  Off by default on purpose: wps_pin (slow, loud, can permanently lock WPS), pmkid_flood (repeated deauth), the WEP enablers (chopchop/fragment/hirte recover keystream, not the key), evil_twin and karma (impersonate an AP), eapol_logoff (transmits a disconnect), deauth_flood/auth_flood/probe_flood/beacon_flood (denial-of-service detection tests) and the situational surveys.  ie_audit/pnl_harvest transmit nothing: add them to any attacks list at no risk (mode="passive" includes them).
_client_mac: deauthenticate this station only (the handshake attack); empty means the whole AP.
_twin_interface: interface the evil twin serves the SSID on; empty = the monitor interface. Put the twin on a second radio to keep the capture running.
_reveal_with_probe: hidden-SSID discovery listens by default; with this on it also asks the AP for the name with a directed probe (the only part of it that transmits).
_pmk_cache: An ESSID-keyed PMK cache: once a passphrase is learned for a network, a later capture of the same ESSID is verified against it instead of being cracked again. Every hit is verified against the capture before it is believed.
_budgets: Per-attack time budget in seconds. attack_timeout > 0 overrides all of them.
_cracking: cracker: auto | aircrack | hashcat. The built-in engine always runs first for targeted candidates.
_environment: kill_interfering stops NetworkManager/wpa_supplicant so injection is reliable; restore_interface puts everything back on exit.
_web: The UI has no authentication: prefer 127.0.0.1 unless you are behind a proxy or a tunnel.
_ai: Optional. No model is required: with ai_provider "none" (or --no-ai/--disable-ai, WIFIPILOT_NO_AI=1, wp.ai(disable=True)) wifipilot runs the deterministic planner and never opens a socket to a model. Otherwise: auto (prefer local Ollama) | ollama | openrouter. Ollama only accepts loopback hosts unless allow_remote_host is set — anything else sends engagement data off the machine. OpenRouter is a cloud service: it stays disabled until you enable it AND provide a key, identifiers are pseudonymised by default and max_cost_usd caps the spend.
